Posted April 25, 2001
Press release April 24, 2001
From The Hassela Nordic Network
http://www.hnnsweden.com

Dutch Health Minister wants hallmark for cannabis products

According to the Dutch daily Algemeen Dagblad today, the Dutch Minister of Health, dr. Els Borst, wants to have a check on what the Dutch label as ‘soft drugs’ that are being sold in coffee shops.

She said that at the so called ‘youth debate’ held on Monday in Parliament. According to the minister, from next year and onwards inspections should be carried out to find out if dangerous pesticides are used in the production of ‘Netherweed’ [Dutch marijuana].
(MarijuanaNews note: Actually, Nederwiet.)

Borst wants to the Food Inspection Department to take on such a task.

However, she wrestles with judicial problems because so-called ‘soft drugs’ are still illegal. Borst doesn’t know yet how to solve this problem. Perhaps agreements with coffee shop owners will be an option.
(MarijuanaNews note: This is one more move toward legalization.)
See
We Are Winning! The Dutch Government Shows More Confidence that Things Are Going Our Way in Europe.

Further, the minister wants coffee shops to inform their customers about their products. She thinks about introduction of labels for joints, at which the amount of tar, nicotine and THC should be stated.
(MarijuanaNews note: The Health Minister should know that there is no nicotine in marijuana. It would be good for everyone to know the THC content, but it would be very difficult to standardize without mass production, which is unlikely for many reasons.)

Borst isn’t much worried by the high THC-content in ‘Netherweed’. Foreign weed has about a five percent THC-content, the Dutch weed 8.5 percent.
See
The Prohibitionists In Stockholm Reveal The Shocking Truth
About The Potency Of Dutch Marijuana

" A high THC-content is in fact a positive quality norm, " Borst said. " You need to smoke less to get the same effect. And that means you get less tar and nicotine in your body. " (Sure Minister – did you know that if you use heroin of good quality you need much less than if you are addicted to Mogadon – that’s Dutch rocket science for you!)
(MarijuanaNews note: Notice their hate for the Dutch. Swedish prohibitionists don’t want children to know that there is a difference between marijuana and heroin. The net result is that deaths due to drug abuse in Sweden are amongst the highest in Europe, having risen from 50 per year in 1970 to 250 per year today. In the age group 20-39, drugs account for 10 percent of all deaths, as many as die in traffic accidents. Holland has the lowest drug related death rate in the EU.)
See

and

and
Swedish European Drug Crusade Collapses

At the youth debate, Borst said that smoking a joint is less harmful for the health than a cigarette.

The Minister of Justice, Korthals, wants to do an experiment where 16- and 17-year-olds should be able to buy cannabis to prevent them from entering the criminal circuit.

Press release April 23, 2001

According to the West Australian newspaper, citing police sources, Ecstasy kits do NOT minimise the harmful effects of drugs and would not be tolerated at dance parties.

According to the promoters of Ecstasy kits, they could save lives. However, the best way to save ‘Ecstasy lives’ is by NOT taking Ecstasy.

HNN-comment: Ecstasy is an illegal drug. It’s illegal because it’s dangerous. It’s not dangerous because it’s illegal. Those taking Ecstasy should be aware of the fact that they might kill themselves. Using drugs is risky, and should remain risky. That’s the price you have to be prepared to pay if you use them. Most things in life involve taking risks – positive and negative risks. If you are prepared to use drugs, drive a car at 150 miles per hour or dive from a cliff – you should be aware of the fact that you might kill yourself. Facilitating illegal drug use by testing illegal drugs is the same as condoning drug use and pushing for its legalisation.
